title: Game-Theoretic Co-Evolution for LLM-Based Heuristic Discovery
claim: A closed iterative loop alternates evaluating populations, computing mixed strategies, and LLM-driven best-response synthesis, then feeds new programs back into the pools.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right, with a bottom feedback arrow looping back
description: A wide three-column diagram on gray panels. The left panel, 'Current Population & Meta-Game', shows two cylinders: a blue Solver Strategy Pool S(t) and a gray Generator Strategy Pool G(t). Each holds stacked code-file icons with gears. Arrows lead from both into an 'Evaluate & Payoff Matrix M^t' box with a blue grid, then into a 'Meta-Solver' box. The meta-solver emits meta-strategies σ_g and σ_s to the middle panel. The middle panel, 'LLM Best-Response Oracles', has a blue Solver box and a gray Generator box. Each contains an LLM swirl icon, a synthesis arrow, a candidate population, and an 'Evaluate against σ' step with a bar-chart icon. A 'Gap Signal' arrow loops back to the LLM. The right panel, 'Strategy Pool Update', shows the new solver s_{t+1} and new generator g_{t+1} as code and document icons. A blue curved arrow along the bottom, labeled 'Next Iteration t → t+1', returns to the left panel.
caption: Overview of ASRO. The iterative process is structured into three phases. (Left) The current solver strategy pool $\mathcal{S}^{(t)}$ and generator strategy pool $\mathcal{G}^{(t)}$ are evaluated pairwise to compute a payoff matrix $M^{(t)}$. A meta-solver then computes mixed meta-strategies $(\sigma_s^{(t)}, \sigma_g^{(t)})$ over the existing strategy pools. (Middle) Program-space best-response oracles synthesize new solver and generator programs conditioned on the opponent’s current meta-strategy, instantiated by an underlying program search mechanism (see Figure [ref]). (Right) The newly discovered solver $s_{t+1}$ and generator $g_{t+1}$ are added to their respective strategy pools for the next iteration ($t \to t+1$), enabling systematic exploration of the program space.
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have enabled rapid progress in automatic heuristic discovery (AHD), yet most existing methods are predominantly limited by static evaluation against fixed instance distributions, leading to potential overfitting and poor generalization under distributional shifts. We propose Algorithm Space Response Oracles (ASRO), a game-theoretic framework that reframes heuristic discovery as a program level co-evolution between solver and instance generator. ASRO models their interaction as a two-player zero-sum game, maintains growing strategy pools on both sides, and iteratively expands them via LLM-based best-response oracles against mixed opponent meta-strategies, thereby replacing static evaluation with an adaptive, self-generated curriculum. Across multiple combinatorial optimization domains, ASRO consistently outperforms static-training AHD baselines built on the same program search mechanisms, achieving substantially improved generalization and robustness on diverse and out-of-distribution instances.
